engXInfSd: Priya's cheeks were red, her mittens were soaked and she was dragging a sled behind her. What can you infer?
She has been sledding in the snow
She has been swimming at the beach
She has been reading indoors
She has been baking cookies
A sled, wet mittens and red cheeks are clues that she was sledding in the snow.
Theo opened the fridge, sighed and closed it again. Then he checked the cupboard and frowned. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
He is hungry but can't find food he wants — he checked the fridge and cupboard
He is cold — he opened the fridge
He is tired — he sighed
He is cleaning — he closed the cupboard
Looking in the fridge and cupboard and frowning shows he wants food but finds nothing he likes.
The classroom was quiet except for pencils scratching. A timer ticked on the teacher's desk. What is most likely happening?
The students are writing a test
The students are at recess
The students are singing a song
The students are eating lunch
Silence, pencils and a timer are clues that students are writing a timed test.
Nadia's dog wagged its tail and ran to the door the moment she picked up the leash. What can you infer about the dog?
It expects to go for a walk
It wants to take a bath
It is afraid of Nadia
It is ready to sleep
Picking up the leash means a walk, and the dog's excitement shows it knows this.
Mr. Lee wiped his forehead, fanned himself with a newspaper and drank three glasses of water. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
It is very hot — he fanned himself and drank lots of water
It is very cold — he wiped his forehead
He is bored — he held a newspaper
He is sleepy — he drank water
Fanning himself and drinking lots of water are clues that he feels hot.
Muddy paw prints led from the back door to the couch, where a wet cushion lay. What most likely happened?
A dog came in from outside and jumped on the couch
Someone spilled juice on the couch
A bird flew through the window
The couch was washed
Muddy paw prints from the door to the couch show an animal came in and climbed up.
Lucas kept looking at the clock, tapping his pencil and glancing at the door during the last class of the day. How does Lucas most likely feel?
Eager for school to end
Interested in the lesson
Sleepy and calm
Proud of his work
Watching the clock and the door shows he can't wait to leave.
Aunt June wore a cap and gown and held a rolled-up paper tied with a ribbon. Everyone was clapping. What can you infer?
She is graduating
She is going swimming
She is starting a new job as a chef
She is moving to a new house
A cap and gown and a rolled diploma are clues of a graduation.
The trees were bare, leaves crunched underfoot and the geese were flying south. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
It is autumn — the geese were flying south
It is summer — the leaves crunched
It is spring — the trees were bare
It is midnight — the geese were flying
Geese fly south and leaves fall in autumn.
Kenji's face lit up when he unwrapped the box, and he immediately put on the new hockey helmet. How does Kenji feel about the gift?
He loves it
He is disappointed
He is confused by it
He wants to return it
His face lit up and he used the helmet right away, showing he loves it.
The lights flickered, the wind howled and Mom handed out candles and flashlights. What can you infer?
A storm might cause the power to go out
It is a sunny afternoon
They are going to a party
Mom is fixing the lights
Flickering lights, howling wind and flashlights suggest a storm and possible power outage.
Hana's backpack was by the door, her lunch was packed and her shoes were on at 7 a.m. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
She is ready for school — her backpack and lunch were ready
She is going to bed — it was 7 a.m.
She is sick — her shoes were on
She is on vacation — her lunch was packed
A packed lunch and a backpack by the door are clues she is ready for school.
The baby's lip trembled, and she reached toward the toy that her brother had just taken. How does the baby most likely feel?
Upset that her toy was taken
Happy to share
Sleepy and calm
Excited to eat
A trembling lip and reaching for the toy show she is upset.
Coach Diaz smiled and wrote Carmen's name at the top of the team list after watching her score three goals in tryouts. What can you infer?
Carmen made the team
Carmen was cut from the team
Carmen quit the team
Carmen is the coach
Scoring three goals and having her name at the top of the list suggests she made the team.
Every shelf in Mrs. Patel's house was full of books, and she carried a novel in her purse. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
She loves reading — her shelves were full of books
She sells purses — she carried a purse
She dislikes books — she had many shelves
She is a carpenter — she built shelves
Full bookshelves and carrying a novel everywhere show she loves to read.
The cookie jar was empty, and crumbs led down the hall to Max's bedroom. What most likely happened?
Max ate the cookies
The cookies were never baked
A neighbour borrowed the jar
The cookies were given away at school
The crumb trail leading to Max's room is a clue that he ate them.
Ruby stared out the car window at the ocean, then the mountains, then the ocean again, and said, "Are we there yet?" for the fifth time. What can you infer?
They are on a long trip
They are going to the corner store
Ruby is asleep
The car is parked at home
Asking "Are we there yet?" many times while scenery changes shows a long trip.
Diego's knees were scraped, his bike lay on the grass and he was wiping his eyes. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
He fell off his bike — his knees were scraped
He won a race — his bike was on the grass
He is laughing — he was wiping his eyes
He is going swimming — he was on the grass
Scraped knees and a bike on the ground are clues that he fell.
The farmer looked at the cracked, dry soil and the wilted corn, then up at the cloudless sky. What can you infer?
The farm needs rain
The farm is flooded
It is the middle of winter
The corn is growing perfectly
Cracked soil, wilted plants and no clouds show a lack of rain.
When Ms. Okafor walked in carrying balloons and a cake, the class shouted, "Surprise!" What can you infer?
The class is having a celebration
The class is having a fire drill
The class is writing a test
School has been cancelled
Balloons, cake and shouting "Surprise!" are clues of a celebration.
Ava held her nose as she walked past the garbage cans in the alley. What can you infer, and which detail supports it?
The garbage smells bad — she held her nose
The garbage is pretty — she walked past
She has a cold — she was in the alley
She is lost — she walked in the alley
Holding her nose is a clue that something smells bad.
Liam's grandfather kept a pair of skates by the door, wore a team jersey and never missed a game on TV. What can you infer about him?
He is a big hockey fan
He dislikes sports
He has never seen a hockey game
He is a basketball player
Skates, a jersey and watching every game show he loves hockey.
engStEl: In a story, which of these is a setting?
a snowy cabin in the mountains
a shy boy named Felix
The cabin door suddenly slams shut.
a clever fox who tells jokes
The setting is where and when a story happens, like a snowy cabin.
In a story, which of these is a character?
a kind teacher named Mr. Brooks
a classroom on the first day of school
Mr. Brooks loses his keys.
a rainy Monday morning
A character is a person or animal in the story.
In a story, which of these is a plot event?
The puppy runs away during the parade.
a fluffy puppy named Biscuit
a small town on parade day
a sunny afternoon in July
A plot event is something that happens in the story.
In a story, which of these is a setting?
a crowded train station at dawn
a nervous traveller with a red suitcase
The train leaves without her.
a friendly conductor
A train station at dawn tells where and when the story happens.
In a story, which of these is a character?
a lonely robot who collects bottle caps
an abandoned junkyard at night
The robot finds a shiny new cap.
a hot summer on a faraway planet
The robot is someone in the story, so it is a character.
In a story, which of these is a plot event?
The twins discover a secret tunnel under the barn.
an old red barn on a farm
two curious twins named Ana and Sol
a foggy autumn evening
Discovering a tunnel is an action that happens, so it is a plot event.
In a story, which of these is the problem?
The team's only goalie breaks her wrist before the final game.
The team wins the trophy at the end.
an ice rink in a small prairie town
a hard-working captain named Jess
The problem is the trouble the characters must solve, like losing their goalie.
In a story, which of these is the solution?
Jess's little brother bravely fills in as goalie.
The goalie breaks her wrist.
a cold arena in January
a team called the Thunderbirds
The solution is how the problem gets solved.
In a story, which of these is a setting?
a tiny island in the middle of a lake
a pirate captain with one boot
The captain buries a chest of gold.
a parrot who repeats everything
An island tells where the story takes place.
In a story, which of these is a character?
a grumpy giant who lives under a bridge
a stone bridge over a rushing river
The giant finally makes a friend.
a misty morning in the valley
The giant is someone in the story, so it is a character.
In a story, which of these is a plot event?
A storm knocks out the power during the sleepover.
Maya's basement on a Friday night
Maya and her best friend Kiara
a flashlight with weak batteries
The storm knocking out the power is something that happens.
In a story, which of these is a setting?
a space station orbiting Mars in 2150
a brave astronaut named Commander Li
The oxygen alarm starts beeping.
a robot helper named Bolt
A space station in 2150 tells where and when.
In a story, which of these is the problem?
Sam's kite gets stuck high in an oak tree.
Sam's dad gets a ladder and frees the kite.
a windy park in spring
a boy named Sam
The stuck kite is the trouble Sam needs to solve.
In a story, which of these is a character?
a wise old turtle who lives in the pond
a muddy pond behind the school
The turtle teaches the frog to be patient.
a hot afternoon in August
The turtle is someone in the story, so it is a character.
In a story, which of these is a plot event?
The princess trades her crown for a magic seed.
a castle high on a cliff
a princess who loves gardening
a long winter in the kingdom
Trading the crown is an action, so it is a plot event.
In a story, which of these is a setting?
a busy bakery on a Saturday morning
a baker with flour on her apron
The bread oven breaks down.
a hungry customer named Raj
A bakery on a Saturday morning tells where and when.
In a story, which of these is the solution?
The villagers work together to rebuild the bridge.
A flood washes away the bridge.
a village beside a wide river
a mayor with a loud voice
Rebuilding the bridge solves the problem caused by the flood.
In a story, which of these is a character?
a mischievous raccoon who steals picnic lunches
a campground in Algonquin Park
The raccoon gets caught in a cooler.
a warm summer night
The raccoon is someone in the story, so it is a character.
In a story, which of these is a plot event?
Grandpa finds an old photo hidden in a book.
Grandpa's dusty attic
a curious girl named Lena
a rainy Sunday afternoon
Finding the photo is something that happens.
In a story, which of these is a setting?
a dinosaur jungle millions of years ago
a baby triceratops named Trix
Trix gets separated from her herd.
a hungry pterodactyl
A prehistoric jungle tells where and when.
In a story, which of these is the problem?
The class hamster escapes the night before the science fair.
The students find the hamster in a boot.
Room 12 at Maple Grove School
a hamster named Peanut
The escape is the trouble that the characters must fix.
In a story, which of these is a character?
a shy new student who loves to draw
a school cafeteria at lunchtime
The new student wins the art contest.
the first week of September
The new student is a person in the story, so she is a character.
engXMyIl: Illustration A shows Hercules wrestling a huge lion. Illustration B shows Hercules wearing the lion's skin as a cloak. What does Illustration B show?
What happens after Hercules defeats the lion
Hercules running from the lion
The lion sleeping in a cave
Hercules meeting the lion for the first time
Wearing the lion's skin shows the fight is already over.
Illustration A shows Arachne weaving a beautiful tapestry. Illustration B shows Arachne as a spider spinning a web. How are the illustrations different?
A shows Arachne as a woman; B shows her as a spider
Both show her as a spider
A shows a spider; B shows a loom
Both show her as a woman
Arachne is a weaver in A and has been turned into a spider in B.
Illustration A shows Medusa with snakes for hair, hiding in a cave. Illustration B shows Perseus holding up a shiny shield in the same cave. What do both illustrations include?
The cave
The shiny shield
Perseus
A winged horse
Both pictures take place in the cave.
Illustration A shows Odin standing on a mountain with two ravens on his shoulders. Illustration B shows the ravens flying over the world. What do both illustrations include?
The two ravens
The mountain
Odin
A sea serpent
Odin appears only in A, but the ravens are in both.
Illustration A shows Orpheus playing his lyre as animals gather to listen. Illustration B shows Orpheus alone and weeping beside a river. How does the mood change from A to B?
From peaceful to sad
From sad to joyful
From angry to calm
It stays the same
A shows a calm, gentle scene and B shows Orpheus weeping.
Illustration A shows Nanabozho paddling a canoe across a calm lake. Illustration B shows him in the same canoe as huge waves crash around him. How are the settings different?
A is a calm lake; B is a stormy lake
A is a desert; B is a forest
Both are calm
Both are stormy
The lake is calm in A and rough with waves in B.
Illustration A shows the Minotaur in the centre of a twisting maze. Illustration B shows Theseus unwinding a ball of thread as he enters the maze. What does Illustration B show that A does not?
Theseus with a ball of thread
The twisting maze
The Minotaur
The centre of the maze
Theseus and his thread appear only in B.
Illustration A shows Narcissus smiling at his reflection in a pond. Illustration B shows a white flower growing by the same pond. What part of the myth does Illustration B show?
The ending, when Narcissus becomes a flower
The beginning, before he sees the pond
Narcissus meeting a friend
A storm over the pond
In the myth, a narcissus flower grows where he once sat.
Illustration A shows Pegasus flying through the clouds. Illustration B shows Pegasus drinking from a mountain spring. How are the illustrations different?
A shows Pegasus in the sky; B shows him on the ground
Both show Pegasus in the sky
A shows a spring; B shows clouds
Both show Pegasus sleeping
Pegasus is flying in A and standing by a spring in B.
Illustration A shows Loki grinning as he hides behind a tree. Illustration B shows the other gods angrily searching the forest. How does Loki most likely feel in Illustration A?
Sneaky and pleased with himself
Frightened and sorry
Sad and lonely
Calm and sleepy
His grin while hiding suggests he is enjoying a trick.
Illustration A shows Athena and Poseidon standing on a hill above a city. Illustration B shows an olive tree growing on the hill while the people cheer. What does Illustration B show?
The people choosing Athena's gift
Poseidon making a flood
The city being built
Athena leaving the city
The cheering crowd and olive tree show Athena's gift won.
Illustration A shows a small Sedna in a kayak with her father. Illustration B shows Sedna at the bottom of the sea surrounded by seals and whales. How are the settings different?
A is on the sea's surface; B is deep under the sea
Both are on land
A is in a forest; B is in a cave
Both are on the surface
The kayak floats on top of the water, while B is on the ocean floor.
Illustration A shows Demeter crying as the fields turn brown and bare. Illustration B shows Demeter smiling as flowers bloom. How does the mood change from A to B?
From sorrowful to joyful
From joyful to sorrowful
From calm to angry
It stays the same
Demeter cries in A and smiles in B.
Illustration A shows Jason's ship, the Argo, sailing toward rocky cliffs. Illustration B shows Jason holding up the golden fleece. What do both illustrations show?
Jason's quest
A dragon sleeping
Jason at home
A battle with giants
Both pictures show parts of Jason's journey to find the fleece.
Illustration A shows Coyote dancing under the stars. Illustration B shows Coyote throwing stars across the sky to make the Milky Way. What part of the story does Illustration B show?
Coyote scattering the stars
Coyote sleeping in a den
Coyote dancing
The sun rising
In B, Coyote is throwing the stars across the sky.
Illustration A shows Prometheus carrying a glowing torch down from a mountain. Illustration B shows people warming their hands around a fire. What does Illustration B show?
What happens after Prometheus brings fire to people
Prometheus climbing the mountain
The gods putting out the fire
People living without fire
People using fire shows the result of Prometheus's gift.
Illustration A shows Thor's hammer lying on the ground. Illustration B shows Thor raising the hammer as lightning flashes. What do both illustrations include?
Thor's hammer
Lightning
Thor
A giant
Only the hammer appears in both pictures.
Illustration A shows the god Ra sailing a golden boat across the daytime sky. Illustration B shows Ra's boat travelling through a dark underworld at night. How are the illustrations different?
A shows day; B shows night
Both show night
A shows the sea; B shows a desert
Both show day
Ra's boat crosses the bright sky in A and the dark underworld in B.
Illustration A shows Echo hiding sadly in the woods. Illustration B shows only a mountain with sound lines bouncing off it. What part of the myth does Illustration B show?
Echo has faded until only her voice remains
Echo meeting Narcissus
Echo singing on stage
Echo climbing the mountain
In the myth, Echo fades away and only her voice is left.
Illustration A shows the hero Maui pulling a rope tied to the sun. Illustration B shows people fishing in long daylight hours. How does Illustration B connect to A?
It shows the result of Maui slowing the sun
It shows Maui before the story starts
It shows the sun escaping
It shows Maui sleeping
Long daylight is the result of Maui slowing the sun.
Illustration A shows King Midas sitting on a golden throne, frowning. Illustration B shows Midas washing his hands in a river and smiling. How does Midas feel in each illustration?
Unhappy in A; happy in B
Happy in both
Unhappy in both
Happy in A; unhappy in B
He frowns in A and smiles in B after losing the golden touch.
Illustration A shows Daedalus building wings from feathers and wax. Illustration B shows Daedalus and Icarus escaping a tower. What do both illustrations include?
Daedalus
The wings melting
The sea
A king
Daedalus appears in both pictures.
engOrgT: A report on bees has the sections Body parts , Homes , Food and Helping plants . Where does "Bees drink nectar from flowers" belong?
Nectar is what bees eat and drink, so it belongs under Food.
A report on bees has the sections Body parts , Homes , Food and Helping plants . Where does "Honeybees build hives with wax" belong?
A hive is where bees live, so it belongs under Homes.
A report on bees has the sections Body parts , Homes , Food and Helping plants . Where does "Pollen sticks to bees and is carried to other flowers" belong?
Carrying pollen helps plants make seeds.
A guide to Canada has the sections Climate , Wildlife , Sports and Languages . Where does "Moose and beavers live in many forests" belong?
Moose and beavers are animals, so this belongs under Wildlife.
A guide to Canada has the sections Climate , Wildlife , Sports and Languages . Where does "English and French are official languages" belong?
This sentence is about languages spoken in Canada.
A guide to Canada has the sections Climate , Wildlife , Sports and Languages . Where does "Winters can drop below minus thirty degrees" belong?
Temperature is about the weather and climate.
A guide to Canada has the sections Climate , Wildlife , Sports and Languages . Where does "Lacrosse is a national summer sport" belong?
A pamphlet on a new puppy has the sections Feeding , Training , Health and Play . Where does "Visit the vet for vaccinations" belong?
Vet visits and vaccinations keep the puppy healthy.
A pamphlet on a new puppy has the sections Feeding , Training , Health and Play . Where does "Reward your puppy when it sits on command" belong?
Teaching commands is part of training.
A pamphlet on a new puppy has the sections Feeding , Training , Health and Play . Where does "Tug toys and fetch burn off energy" belong?
Toys and fetch are ways to play.
A report on the solar system has the sections The Sun , Planets , Moons and Space exploration . Where does "Jupiter is the largest planet" belong?
A report on the solar system has the sections The Sun , Planets , Moons and Space exploration . Where does "Astronauts first walked on the Moon in 1969" belong?
Astronauts travelling into space is space exploration.
A report on the solar system has the sections The Sun , Planets , Moons and Space exploration . Where does "Titan is the largest moon of Saturn" belong?
An essay on healthy habits has the sections Sleep , Eating , Exercise and Screen time . Where does "Turn off devices an hour before bed" belong?
Turning off devices is about limiting screen time.
An essay on healthy habits has the sections Sleep , Eating , Exercise and Screen time . Where does "Children need about ten hours of rest each night" belong?
Hours of rest at night is about sleep.
An essay on healthy habits has the sections Sleep , Eating , Exercise and Screen time . Where does "Fill half your plate with vegetables" belong?
What goes on your plate is about eating.
A report on rainforests has the sections Layers , Animals , Plants and Threats . Where does "Logging destroys millions of trees each year" belong?
Logging is a danger to rainforests, so it is a threat.
A report on rainforests has the sections Layers , Animals , Plants and Threats . Where does "The canopy is the thick top layer of leaves" belong?
The canopy is one of the rainforest's layers.
A report on rainforests has the sections Layers , Animals , Plants and Threats . Where does "Sloths hang upside down from branches" belong?
A business plan for a lemonade stand has the sections Supplies , Prices , Location and Advertising . Where does "Make bright posters to hang around the neighbourhood" belong?
Posters tell people about the stand, which is advertising.
A business plan for a lemonade stand has the sections Supplies , Prices , Location and Advertising . Where does "Set up near the park entrance" belong?
Where the stand goes is its location.
A business plan for a lemonade stand has the sections Supplies , Prices , Location and Advertising . Where does "Each cup will cost one dollar" belong?
The cost of a cup is its price.
engTrBs: Choose the best transition. The snow was very deep. ___, school was closed for the day.
School closing is a result of the deep snow.
Choose the best transition. Owls hunt at night. ___, hawks hunt during the day.
The sentences contrast owls and hawks.
Choose the best transition. First, pour the milk into a pot. ___, heat it slowly.
Heating comes after pouring, so it is the next step.
Choose the best transition. Many animals hibernate. ___, bears sleep through much of the winter.
Bears are an example of animals that hibernate.
Choose the best transition. I wanted to go to the beach. ___, it started to rain.
Rain is the opposite of what was wanted, so the sentences show contrast.
Choose the best transition. Biking is good exercise. ___, it does not pollute the air.
The second sentence adds another benefit.
Choose the best transition. We packed, loaded the car and drove for hours. ___, we arrived at the cottage.
Arriving is the last step in the sequence.
Choose the best transition. Leo forgot to water his plant. ___, its leaves turned brown.
The brown leaves were caused by not watering.
Choose the best transition. Some fruits are very sour. ___, lemons make your mouth pucker.
Lemons are an example of a sour fruit.
Choose the best transition. My brother loves loud music. ___, I prefer quiet songs.
The sentences show two different preferences.
Choose the best transition. ___, wash your hands. Next, gather the ingredients.
Washing your hands is the first step before "Next".
Choose the best transition. Reading builds your vocabulary. ___, it can take you to new places in your imagination.
The second sentence adds another reason reading is good.
Choose the best transition. The bridge was icy. ___, drivers went very slowly.
Drivers slowed down because the bridge was icy.
Choose the best transition. Penguins are birds. ___, they cannot fly.
Not flying is surprising for a bird, so the sentences show contrast.
Choose the best transition. We had a fun day at the zoo. ___, we saw the giraffes eat lunch.
Seeing giraffes eat is an example of the fun day.
Choose the best transition. Plant the seed in soil. ___, water it every day.
Choose the best transition. The movie was long. ___, it was exciting from start to finish.
"Even so" shows that the movie was exciting despite being long.
Choose the best transition. Recycling saves resources. ___, it keeps garbage out of landfills.
The second sentence adds another benefit of recycling.
Choose the best transition. Maya studied every night. ___, she got an excellent mark.
Her excellent mark came from studying.
Choose the best transition. Tomatoes can be grown in many ways. ___, some people grow them in pots on balconies.
Growing tomatoes in pots is one example of a way to grow them.
Choose the best transition. Frogs live in water when they are young. ___, they can live on land as adults.
The sentences describe a change over time.
Choose the best transition. Cats like to nap in the sun. ___, my dog prefers the cool basement.
The sentences contrast what cats and the dog like.
